newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela expects over five pct growth this year.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela expects over five pct growth this year.

text.p: The Venezuelan economy is expected to grow more than five percent in 1997, after a 1.6 percent contraction last year, the government said on Sunday.
The forecast was contained in a Planning Ministry report, a presidential palace release said.
"The Cordiplan (Planning Ministry) report forecasts a growth of the gross domestic product of more than five percent for 1997," the statement said.

Earlier government economic growth estimates were between 3.5 and four percent. Meanwhile, state-owned oil giant Petroleos de Venezuela (PdVSA) has forecast 5.8 percent growth for 1997, rising to 7.8 percent in 1998.
Finance Ministry figures in April showed non-oil GDP growing by 2.0 percent, while the oil economy would rise 6.9 percent.

The report quoted by the presidency said the over five percent growth estimate could be expected following "a 10 percent increase in private sector exports during the first quarter, a rise in investments in the manufacturing sector ... and higher electricity consumption."
